items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: that was a smaller group of some members of your band and some white musicians, namely, Max Kominski

ctx.x: Well, whatever he thought, I think he had much more to say, and he should have continued.

Then, now we return to that Chocolate Dandies date we mentioned in October of 1933, which was the first recordings with Teddy Wilson, and then a few days later . . . that was a smaller group of some members of your band and some white musicians, namely, Max Kominski [phonetic] and Floyd O’Brien [phonetic] and, reputedly, Mez Mezro [phonetic] banging on the drums somewhere, but that’s not confirmed. But, do you remember, was this another idea of John Hammond, to sort of have an integrated recording unit?
